name: ɬəw̓ál̓məš
catalog_citation: Robertson, David Douglas. 2014. ɬəw̓ál̓məš (Lower Chehalis) morphosyntax. Papers for the International Conference on Salish and Neighbouring Languages 49 (UBCWPL), 89-153.
catalog_locator: p.90 (sec. 1, root shape and stress); p.124 (lexical suffixes); p.131 (náw= prefix); pp.133-135 (reduplication, stress-attracting •V́C); p.150 (future research…
catalog_quote: We preface this discussion by observing that roots in ɬəw̓ál̓məš are typically of the form CV́C, CV́CC or alternating Cə́RC/CəRV́C. All things being equal, roots tend to remain stressed regardless of morphological operations on them. There are however exceptions, which we have not as yet systematically worked out. The reader is referred to Snow (1969) for the best extant summary. ... Many of these suffixes have several variant forms not necessarily predictable by phonological rules. The stress on these suffixes may be variable. These affixes need much more research. ... náw= 'big' (takes primary stress; the stem it modifies takes secondary stress) ... Our arbitrary working assumption is that, barring other evidence, it is the root that is stressed in the resulting form, with the copied material unstressed. (Vowels in unstressed syllables may reduce to schwa.) ... It is not yet known how…

sources.citation: Robertson, David Douglas. 2024. "At the Neighbors'": The etymology of "Chinook", language contact, and intangible cultural heritage. Papers for ICSNL 59 (UBCWPL), 482-500.
sources.quote: Of Lower Chehalis interrogative/deictic roots: 'While these are stressed, as we expect roots to be, the data from one Tsamosan language, Qn, additionally include certain words ... bearing an unstressed prefix kə-'; also p.~495 an 'unstressed Lo prefix' nəkʷ- 'together'. Consistent with root-anchored stress and unstressed grammatical prefixes.

sources.citation: Robertson, David Douglas. 2015. P.S.: more Lower Chehalis loans in Chinook Jargon, and ɬəw̓ál̓məš revitalization. Papers for ICSNL 50 (UBCWPL 40).
sources.quote: No statement on Lower Chehalis word stress; single mention concerns a Chinookan unstressed gender prefix reduced to schwa in a loan.

sources.citation: Kinkade, M. Dale. 1979. Preliminary notes on Lower Chehalis (ɬəw̓ál̓məš) morphology. Papers for the 14th International Conference on Salish Languages, 108-119.
sources.quote: Only stress content: one root type (C-a-Resonant-C) has aspectual variants — 'The continuative of such roots has the stressed vowel preceding the resonant (CaRá- [sic scanned]), the completive has it after (CaRáC-, with an epenthetic vowel before the resonant)', e.g. ʔi-láik-n 'he is falling' / ta laiák-w 'he fell'. No general stress rule stated.
sources.locator: sec. 3.1 Aspect, paper-internal p.4 (two-up scan, scanned text layer)
sources.note: Second of the two Glottolog descriptive refs; fetched sources now — adds only the CaRá-/CáRaC aspectual stress alternation in resonant roots, no general rule; keep on file as corroboration of root-internal stress alternation.
